output_list.reason: The distributeTokens function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The issue is in the for loop where the reward is calculated: 'uint reward = balanceOf[holder] * 3 / 100;'. If the balanceOf[holder] is large, the reward will overflow and become very small, allowing the owner to steal the funds.

The transfer function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The issue is in the following code: 'if (balanceOf[msg.sender] < _value) throw; if (balanceOf[_to] + _value < balanceOf[_to]) throw;'. If the balanceOf[msg.sender] is very small, the function will overflow and not revert, allowing attackers to transfer arbitrary tokens.

The transferFrom function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The issue is in the following code: 'if (balanceOf[_from] < _value) throw; if (balanceOf[_to] + _value < balanceOf[_to]) throw;'. If the balanceOf[_from] is very small, the function will overflow and not revert, allowing attackers to transfer arbitrary tokens from any user.

The mintToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. The issue is in the following code: 'balanceOf[target] += mintedAmount; totalSupply += mintedAmount;'. If mintedAmount is large, the balanceOf[target] will overflow and become very small, allowing the owner to steal the funds.
The mintToken function has a wrong logic vulnerability. The mintedAmount is minted to the target without any check, allowing the owner to mint tokens to any address, causing severe token devaluation.
